notes: As of 2026-11-04 ~11:00 ET; election counts incomplete. Margins are D minus R in percentage points; overperformance = candidate margin minus same-state presidential margin (most recent presidential election on or before the race; 2026 races vs 2024). State pres margins for 2016/2020/2024 come from the project's parsed Wikipedia presidential results (scratch pres_parsed.json); 2008/2012 baselines (CA, NJ, CT, KY, IN) were entered from the cited Wikipedia pages without re-fetch. Track-record entries carry verified_by_fetch_this_session; unverified pre-2026 margins come from the cited Wikipedia election pages and should be spot-checked. Wave context: Wikipedia (2026 Senate elections, projected) shows Democrats gaining 7-9 Senate seats (flips in TX, NC, OH special, IA, SC, KS, ME) and a projected House majority; every 2028-relevant Democrat on the ballot won. Style labels for non-candidates rely partly on pre-June-2026 knowledge plus 2026 coverage; confidence flags reflect that. Favorability: no single national poll covered all names; national RV/LV figures used where found (Harvard/Harris Oct 24-26; Echelon Oct 15-19); otherwise Liberal Currents Democratic-voters-only numbers (flagged in population). Primary polls show Harris leading (RCP avg 24.2) while markets price Ossoff first (Polymarket 29.4, Kalshi 21 as of ~11:13 AM ET) despite his no-run pledge. Declined per Wikipedia 2028 primaries page: Ossoff, Talarico, Moore, El-Sayed, Walz ('never run for elected office again'), Polis, Sanders, Michelle Obama; included anyway where markets/polls still price them. Excluded from main list: Tim Walz (declined; 0.1% markets), Chris Van Hollen, Josh Stein, Roy Cooper (NC Senate winner per Wikipedia map), Sherrod Brown (OH special winner per map), Adam Hamilton (KS Senate winner; ~0.4-0.6% markets). WebSearch budget for the run was exhausted mid-task; Ohio governor, Maine Senate details, California wealth-tax outcome and several candidates' midterm activities were not verified.
